INDUNA - FAVOURITE COLOURS (RELEASE SHOW)
Following recent performances supporting internationally acclaimed Nigerian artist Seun Kuti & Egypt 80, Aotearoa-based South African artist InDuna is set to release his new single 'Favourite Colours' and celebrates with a special headline show at Moon, Newtown, Wellington on Friday 30th October 2026.

Blending Afro-pop, R&B and folk, InDuna's live show brings infectious rhythms and uplifting energy alongside the more personal stories behind the songs. 'Favourite Colours' is an atmospheric anthem about identity, healing and resilience, using colour as a metaphor for how anxiety, grief and disconnection can drain the vibrancy from life, and the journey back to yourself.

﻿
InDuna will be joined by a special guest support act, to be announced.


Wheelchair accessible, seated and standing available.


About InDuna

Artist and producer InDuna draws on his South African roots, raised between Johannesburg and Limpopo before moving to Aotearoa at fourteen. His sound fuses African rhythm with contemporary pop and electronic production. Highlights include the King's Trust Young Global Achiever Award (2024), his single 'Dreams' (Best Original Song, International Online Web Fest; Official NZ Hot Singles Chart; featured in 'Ink and Gold'), and his 2025 EP 'Go High' (#16, Official Top 20 Aotearoa Albums Chart). He's supported Seun Kuti & Egypt 80 and opened for JessB, Estère and Deva Mahal, with headline shows across Wellington and Auckland.

'Favourite Colours' is supported by New Zealand On Air.

Summer Meltdown '27

SUMMER MELTDOWN - We're set to ignite your summer with an unforgettable fusion of sound, energy, and culture.

﻿

Bringing you a powerhouse lineup featuring Aotearoa's most iconic artists, SIX60, Katchafire, The Black Seeds, Troy Kingi, Ria Hall and Tiki Taane. This is the moment music fans have been waiting for - and the countdown to one of summer's biggest festivals starts right now!

﻿

TICKET DATES

Pre-sale: Thursday 10th Sept, 8am

Public Sale: Friday 11th Sept, 8am

﻿

SIX60

Returning to Wellington for the first time in 2 years to headline Summer Meltdown, SIX60's story has always felt larger than life, and their music even more so. What began as Dunedin flatmates jamming for fun has evolved into a sound that's unmistakably their own. Get ready for a full-scale spectacle of inescapable anthems.




KATCHAFIRE

Katchafire's journey from the mighty H-Town to the world stage is rooted in pure Māori pride and classic reggae spirit. Blending vibrant rhythms and uplifting grooves with cultural depth, Katchafire bring an authentic, soul-soaked reggae experience to Summer Meltdown.




THE BLACK SEEDS

Returning to their Wellington roots, The Black Seeds bring their reputation for irresistible grooves, signature warmth, rhythm and world-class energy to the Summer Meltdown stage with a live show that hits with big-beat funk, dub, soul and roots-reggae.

﻿

TROY KINGI

One of Aoteraroa's most creative artists, Troy Kingi's 10/10/10 project - ten albums, ten genres, ten years - has earned major accolades and cemented his position as a fearless creative force. Performing with his live band, The Cactus Handshake, Kingi brings a genre-shifting, bold and boundary-defying show to Brewtown.




RIA HALL

One of the country's most compelling voices, Ria Hall effortlessly blends hip-hop, reggae, soul, dancehall ragga and modern beats into a sound that's vibrant and fearless. A powerful live performer shaped by kapa haka and dedicated to elevating te reo Māori, Ria delivers a fierce and deeply soulful set.




TIKI TAANE

With a career that has been defined by innovation, creativity and a deep connection to live performance, Tiki Taane is undoubtedly one of Aotearoa's most influential and versatile artists. When Tiki steps onto the Summer Meltdown stage he'll unleash an immersive, live looping, high-energy one man band set that showcases the iconic energy that has made him a cornerstone of New Zealand music.

Huge anthems, massive performances, and a full-throttle celebration of the music that makes New Zealand unique.

Conference Theme:
At the Confluence: Communities, Catchments, and our Freshwater Futures - Ngā Rerenga E Tūtaki Ana

Our 2026 conference explores the confluence: the place where flows meet, merge, and reshape one another. In freshwater science, confluences are dynamic hydrological junctions which create unique habitats and environments. For this conference it represents the meeting of people, knowledge systems, innovations, and aspirations that shape the future of wai in Aotearoa.

Hosting the conference in Te Whanganui‑a‑Tara/Wellington, where urban streams like Waimapihi and Kumutoto meet the great harbour Te Whanganui‑a‑Tara provides a powerful metaphor for integration across urban waters, catchments, and communities. As Aotearoa navigates changing climate pressures, evolving policy landscapes, disruptive technologies, and growing community involvement, this confluence becomes a space for meaningful collaboration and forward‑thinking action.

We look forward to welcoming you to WLG!

Inhabiting a mind or body that society often refuses to accommodate is a life's work. Fighting the prejudices that make that difficult is an act of political rebellion, one that is capable of unleashing great joy.

Join Deaf and disabled writers for readings and kōrero that will annihilate the ableist tropes between them and their good times. Emcee Olivia Shivas (editor of The D*List) will lead a panel including writer/librarians Riah Tahana-Dawson (Ngāti Kurī, Ngāti Waikato-Tainui) and Bee Trudgeon, and writer/actor/filmmaker Jared Flitcroft (Ngāti Maniapoto).

The Politics of Disabled Joy is curated by the Crip the Lit rōpū, which advocates for placing the unique voices and perspectives of Deaf and disabled writers within a mainstream writing context

long_description:
Papa M & Mick Turner | Wellington
Two of the most distinctive guitarists in independent music come together for an intimate double bill this October.
﻿
Over the past four decades, David Pajo and Mick Turner have quietly shaped the sound of experimental rock, post-rock and instrumental music through an extraordinary body of work. Between them they've played in, recorded with or collaborated alongside artists including Slint, Dirty Three, Tortoise, Gang of Four, Cat Power, Interpol, Yeah Yeah Yeahs, Bonnie 'Prince' Billy, Stereolab, Royal Trux and countless others, leaving an influence that reaches far beyond their own recordings.

﻿Performing as Papa M, David Pajo has spent more than 25 years exploring the expressive possibilities of the electric guitar, moving effortlessly between shimmering instrumentals, folk songwriting and expansive, cinematic compositions. His latest album, Ballads of Harry Houdini, marks another bold chapter, weaving together intricate guitar work, textured electronics and vocals into what Drag City describes as "a fresh, fine and fat-assed set of songs."

﻿As a founding member of Dirty Three, Mick Turner helped redefine instrumental rock, developing a guitar style that's instantly recognisable: lyrical, spacious and emotionally direct. Alongside his acclaimed solo recordings and work with Tren Brothers and Mess Esque, Turner has built a catalogue that rewards careful listening and continues to inspire musicians around the world.

﻿Twenty-six years after first touring Australia and New Zealand together, Papa M and Mick Turner reunite for a rare run of intimate performances. Whether you've followed their work for decades or are discovering it for the first time, this is a rare opportunity to experience two singular artists whose influence can be heard across generations of independent music.

long_description:
Business Training New Zealand Leadership & Management Part 3 Workshop
Our Leadership & Management Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people in a leadership/management position.

About this Event



Leaders today are expected to be the driving force of their teams. They are constantly under pressure to lead effectively in a business environment that is characterised by constant change. Our leadership and management courses offer participants the opportunity to develop the necessary skills to embrace this challenge and lead their teams through these times with confidence and pride.

Our Leadership & Management - Part 3 workshop is a practical skills training course designed for people already in a leadership/management position, or those about to take up a new role, who want to explore the latest thinking and models for effective management and leadership and build on the techniques acquired in our Part 1 and 2 workshops.

In today’s world, emotional Intelligence is a critical and powerful component of effective leadership. This 2-day course will equip leaders with the skills to become more ‘people smart’ by developing ways to lead with emotional intelligence. Participants will also learn how to inspire their people with a shared vision and align teams to company goals, along with the tools to lead and manage change, ways to become a more influential and persuasive leader and the tools to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace.

Course Outcomes

Assess your leadership strengths and identify opportunities for growth
Learn how to become a more inspirational and influential leader
Understand the importance of emotional intelligence as a key leadership skill
Learn how to lead with emotional intelligence, develop leadership self-awareness and become more ‘people smart’
Communicate your goals, vision and purpose with greater clarity, confidence and inspiration
Inspire and align your team to your shared vision and goals
Understanding change and learn how to lead change and growth in your organisation
Apply strategies to motivate and inspire your people to embrace change and strive for positive outcomes
Understand what unconscious bias is and recognise its effects on your people and your organisation
Explain how you can manage your own unconscious bias and implement steps to raise awareness and manage unconscious bias in the workplace

Course Prerequisite: Participants must have a good understanding of leadership and management fundamentals and/or have previously attended the Business Training New Zealand - Leadership & Management Part 1 & 2 course.

For more information or to book: email or call 04 974 8790

long_description:
Summer Tour - Kāpiti
Don't miss some Baroque French and Italian delights with NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen and Aotearoa New Zealand soprano Anna Leese.

It is astonishing to consider the musical impact Giovanni Pergolesi made, considering he died of tuberculosis at the age of 26. Like Mozart, his early demise quickly became the stuff of legend — hundreds of works were (often falsely) ascribed to this Italian late-Baroque genius, while rumours swirled that his death was the result of murderous jealousy from musical rivals.

Led by NZSO Concertmaster Vesa-Matti Leppänen, we survey some of Pergolesi’s most brilliant opera — La serva padrona, Adriano in Siria, L’Olimpiade and Il prigionier superbo. We are delighted to have Aotearoa New Zealand soprano Anna Leese join us as we delve into music that glories in resplendent Italian Baroque colours and textures.

We complete this magnificent concert with a detour into the French-Baroque, with a suite from Jean-Philippe Rameau's Platée. C’est magnifique!

Generously supported by Ainsley Walter

Would you like to become less busy and more productive? Then our Time Management workshop is for you.

About this Event



You've all heard the expression 'Time is money' Well actually time is more valuable than money because time is a non renewable resource. Do you ever have those times when you've been busy all day but feel that you have not achieved what you need to?

Effective Time Management is crucial in today's busy and competitive world. Successes and failures in work and daily activities largely depend on how time is managed. Therefore Time Management is the number one skill to master.

Do you ever feel overwhelmed by the sheer volume of work to be done? Would you like to become less busy and more productive? Then our Time Management workshop is for you. Let us show you and your organisation how to get the most out of a day with better time management skills.

WORKSHOP OBJECTIVES

Plan and prioritise each day’s activities in a more efficient and productive manner
Overcome procrastination quickly and easily
Handle crises effectively and quickly
Organise your workspace and workflow to make better use of time
Become less stressed, less busy and more productive
Delegate more efficiently
Handle interruptions and beat time wasters
Use rituals to make your life run smoother
Plan meetings more appropriately and effectively

Time management training most often begins with setting goals. These goals are recorded and may be broken down into a project, an action plan, or a simple task list. Activities are then rated based on urgency and importance, priorities assigned, and deadlines set.

This process results in a plan with a task list or calendar of activites. Routine and recurring tasks are often given less focus to free time to work on tasks that contribute to important goals. This entire process is supported by a skill set that includes personal motivation, delegation skills, organisational tools and crisis management tools.
